input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Reusing one statistics dictionary makes nested and overlapping invocations overwrite each other's statistics. The async wrapper introduces the same loss of per-call isolation.
- rationale: For example, a function using stop_after_attempt(3) can call itself with an argument that succeeds immediately, then raise on each outer attempt. Every inner call clears and resets the dictionary shared with the active outer call, so the final outer statistics report attempt_number=1 despite three outer attempts. Previously, each invocation's retry controller had its own statistics dictionary. Concurrent async calls likewise corrupt each other's reported statistics.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is shared and cleared on every call, so nested or overlapping invocations overwrite each other's start_time and attempt_number. It gives a nested-call example, mentions concurrent async calls, and notes that each call previously had its own dict.
